description.value: Liard River Hot Springs is home to the second largest hot spring in Canada, set within a lush boreal spruce forest of national ecological significance. The Alpha pool sits at the end of a boardwalk that winds through a warm-water swamp and old-growth forest, making it a remarkable natural detour for cyclists touring the Alaska Highway. The park is open year-round and is one of the most popular stopovers on the entire Alaska Highway corridor.

address.value: Km 765 Alaska Highway, Liard River, V0C 1Z0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The BC Parks website confirms Liard River Hot Springs Park is an active, year-round provincial park at Km 765 of the Alaska Highway. Facilities explicitly listed are a change house and composting toilet (confirming washrooms), but no bike parking, potable water, or cycling-specific amenities are mentioned. OSM tags (bath:open_air=yes, bath:type=hot_spring) align perfectly with the website description of the Alpha pool outdoor hot spring.
concerns: No phone number present in OSM record; BC Parks general line (1-800-689-9025) is available on the contact page but is not park-specific.
No explicit mention of bike parking or potable drinking water on the park page — these amenities cannot be confirmed or denied from available evidence.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A landmark natural attraction on the Alaska Highway popular with touring cyclists; the second largest hot spring in Canada and a well-documented, year-round provincial park. A clear WWC directory fit.
enrichment_extras.notes: The staffed gatehouse doubles as a local visitor centre during the day-use fee season (May 1–September 30), which may offer additional amenities not listed on the website.

wow_evidence: Canada's second-largest hot spring in an ecologically significant boreal swamp, boardwalk to the Alpha pool — intrinsically among Canada's great natural soaks; Alaska Highway riders plan around it (delight-4 band even before any scarcity uplift).
